extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and beginning reporters (especially those learning to write editorials and sports reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing formal news editorials and for related sports reporting (leads, headlines, play-by-play, box features, interviews). Emphasizes organization, factual grounding, clarity, and appropriate use of vernacular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of a formal news editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple plan for organizing a formal news editorial: (1) State briefly the situation that stimulated the editorial (summarize the facts out of which the editorial grows). (2) Explain, interpret or digest; comment or give opinion; argue for or against. (3) Make the point briefly (the writer’s deduction from his exposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the three-part structure: brief situational statement, development (interpretation/argument), and a concise point/conclusion. Keep exposition logical and focused on facts that prompted the editorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions in writing editorials
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't preach; don't change the person from third to second; don't comment in generalities; write simply and specifically; give specific authorities for statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid moralizing tone ('preach'), avoid shifting grammatical person which breaks tone, avoid vague generalities—support claims with named authorities or concrete evidence. Maintain simple, specific prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial must grow out of the news and show logical thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial must be a timely essay that grows out of the news of the day; the comment or interpretation omitted from a news article may find expression in the editorial. Logical thinking must be the basis of all editorials; they must be written in clear direct style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor opinion pieces in recent factual events; ensure the editorial adds interpretation or argument grounded in those facts and follows clear logical reasoning presented in direct language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial development and placement of proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Development: (1) state the proposition in the first sentence of the development; (2) present clear, direct, convincing facts in support of the proposition; (3) suggest alternatives where appropriate; (4) be terse in making the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin development with the proposition, follow with tightly arranged supporting facts, offer alternatives if relevant, and finish with a terse, memorable point. Incorporate the stimulating fact briefly in the opening sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sport headline principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The sport head should tell the news concretely and in the vernacular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write sports headlines that state the essential news plainly and use accepted game vocabulary (vernacular) rather than slang or ambiguous phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports leads: concrete elements and appropriate vernacular
rubrics_metrics.description: Leads should include the concrete elements that tell the news and use game vernacular appropriately; distinguish vernacular from cheap slang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or writing a sports lead, list the concrete facts that communicate the event (who, what, where, when, key figure/action). Use sport-specific terminology where it clarifies action, but avoid gratuitous or flippant slang.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus and construction of sport stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze what is played up in each story; identify the angle emphasized and how the article is constructed to support that emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess which facts, players, plays, or themes the story foregrounds and check that the structure (lead, development, key quotes, statistics) supports that angle coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospect/team preview criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing a season prospect: get a schedule of games, give facts about the players, and note past achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the team's upcoming schedule, player biographies/statistics, and historical performance to contextualize expectations; rely on verifiable facts rather than speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play-by-play reporting accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Go to any game and write it up play by play following the directions given (i.e., accurate chronological account).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, sequential account of the action, using precise verbs and concrete details (who did what, when). Ensure timing, scoring, and sequence are correct and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box feature as by-product
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a box feature as a by-product of the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the game's facts and statistics produce a concise box feature (summaries, standout performances, contextual nuggets) that complements the main report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player interview preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Get an interview with a team's most brilliant player; prepare questions you would want him to answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design questions to elicit informative, revealing answers about performance, preparation, decision-making, and context—avoid yes/no questions and aim for quotes that illuminate the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sport-specific vocabulary mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a list of all minor sports and write five verbs needed to describe action peculiar to each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For accurate and vivid reporting, learn the specialized action verbs and terms for each sport covered so descriptions are precise and idiomatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial analysis: incorporate stimulating facts in opening and use development to justify point
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, brief statement of facts that stimulated the editorial should be skillfully incorporated in the opening sentence; development should bring out what is significant in the report and support the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the opening anchors the editorial in a specific factual stimulus; use subsequent paragraphs to unpack significance and lead naturally to the editorial's concise point.

rubrics_metrics.name: News selection and editing principle (production constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compilation of a newspaper involves selection: telegraph/type-direct transmission would bypass necessary editing—news dispatches must be condensed and edited so the paper prints a correlated composite picture of the day's events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that speed must be balanced with editorial selection and condensation; editors should preserve essentials while shaping dispatches for readability and space, rather than printing raw incoming copy verbatim.
